S7 Class for the Jeffreys Penalty

Source: R/jeffreys.R
JeffreysPenalty.Rd

JeffreysPenalty is the subclass of penalties7::penalty() that a jfp() term attaches to its block. It carries the power of the determinant and the setting of the constant direction, and it has no hyperparameters.

Usage

JeffreysPenalty(
  penalty_name = character(0),
  map = NULL,
  n_coef = integer(0),
  params = character(0),
  params_bounds = list(),
  link_params = list(),
  params_smooth = logical(0),
  power = integer(0),
  intercept = NULL
)

jeffreys_penalty(n_coef, power = 0.5, intercept = NULL)

Arguments

penalty_name, map, params, params_bounds, link_params, params_smooth

Properties inherited from penalties7::penalty(). The penalty has no map and no hyperparameters, so jeffreys_penalty() sets the name "jeffreys", map = NULL, an empty params, empty lists of bounds and links, and an empty logical params_smooth.

n_coef

The number of coefficients in the block.

power

The power \(a\) of the determinant, a single positive number.

intercept

NULL, TRUE or FALSE, the setting of the constant direction (see jfp()).

Value

jeffreys_penalty() returns an S7 object of class JeffreysPenalty, inheriting from penalties7::penalty().

Details

The penalty is \(-a\log|\tilde I(\beta)|\), where \(\tilde I\) is the expected Fisher information of the block's coefficients, augmented by the constant direction of the formula level where jfp() includes it. That matrix depends on the family and on every predictor of the model, so the penalty cannot be evaluated from the block's coefficients alone, and the methods of penalties7::penalty_value(), penalties7::penalty_gradient(), penalties7::penalty_hessian() and of the other generics that read the coefficients signal an error. The fitting layer evaluates it on the model.

The methods that do not need the model return their answer: penalties7::penalty_kinks() is empty, penalties7::is_proper() and penalties7::is_quadratic() are FALSE.

See also

jfp(), the term that attaches it.

Examples

p <- jeffreys_penalty(3)
p@power
#> [1] 0.5
p@params
#> character(0)
penalties7::penalty_kinks(p, list())
#> numeric(0)
penalties7::is_proper(p)
#> [1] FALSE
